answer: Each agent claims one juniper tree beside an oasis well, posts a 70-credit bond, and pays a drawdown fee. A juniper sap-flow sensor and a ferrous pipe meter record each withdrawal; an auditor recomputes well level from both logs and burns the bond on a reused reading, double claim, or shortfall. The first claim costs 31 credits, the kth costs 31+6(k-1), so the 1000th costs 6025 and 1000 fake claims cost 3,028,000 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-well ring fails because one sensor cannot show two simultaneous drawdowns. An honest agent pays 31 once and keeps the bond after a clean audit.
